Rather than touch `CalendarExportOutcome` (Claude B's file this round), I gave the generic-failure case its own honest alert in my own file — keeps the four real outcome states meaning exactly what they say.

**Built the iPad two-pane split** — a locked must-have, unowned for six rounds, and squarely navigation/layout. `DayView` now checks `horizontalSizeClass` (not idiom or screen width) and renders a genuine `NavigationSplitView` with the stop list as sidebar and `DayMapView` as detail when regular-width, instead of the phone's mode-switched single pane. Both panes share the existing `selectedStopID` binding, so tapping a list row or a map pin works simultaneously in both, not toggled between — real independent-pane interaction, not a stretched phone layout. Compact width keeps the existing list/map toggle unchanged.

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Live Activity is real now, built end-to-end but not yet wired to any trigger — same disciplined "standalone, flag the hand-off" pattern that's worked cleanly for Settings and Packing.

**Extracted `NextStopResolver.swift`** before it got duplicated a third time — the "current-or-next stop" rule lived inline in `NextStopWidget`'s provider (my code from round 4), and Live Activity needed the identical logic. Pulled it into a shared function in `WaypointKit`, refactored `NextStopWidget.swift` to use it, added 6 unit tests covering the edge cases (checked-off stops, lapsed windows, no-time-set stops, empty day).

**`LiveActivityController.swift` + `TripActivityAttributes.swift`** — new `LiveActivity/` folder in `WaypointKit`. Matches the interface contract exactly: checks `ActivityAuthorizationInfo().areActivitiesEnabled` before ever calling `Activity.request`, every request uses `pushType: nil` (the actual enforcement point for "no server-push updates, ever"), and a failed/unsupported/denied request is a silent no-op — never a crash, never a fake "started" state.

**`WaypointWidget/TripLiveActivity.swift`** — the actual Dynamic Island/lock-screen content, using `Text(timerInterval:)` per the locked design so the countdown updates continuously without waking the app. Caught a real crash risk while building this: `Text(timerInterval:)` needs a non-inverted date range, but since updates only fire on real state changes (not a per-minute timer), a stale content state's `nextStopTime` can end up in the past by the time the view re-renders — a naive `Date()...nextStopTime` would crash the widget process at that point. Added a `countdownRange` clamp (`now...max(target, now)`) so a stale countdown just shows 0:00 instead.

**Left for the integrator, explicitly:** `WaypointWidgetBundle.swift` needs `TripLiveActivity()` added alongside `NextStopWidget()` in its `body` — that file's `@main` entry point, not mine to touch. And `Info.plist` needs `NSSupportsLiveActivities = YES` or `Activity.request` will never succeed — same pattern as `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` last round, please add both together.

**Left for Claude A/primary_ui, explicitly:** nothing calls `LiveActivityController.start/update/end` yet.
